CLM-EDA-0008.statement: The base testbench for the Async FIFO design achieves a functional coverage of 91.7% by hitting 33 out of 36 bins.

CLM-EDA-0009.statement: The base testbench for the UART TX design achieves a functional coverage of 88.9% by hitting 16 out of 18 bins.

CLM-EDA-0010.statement: The base testbench for the AHB2APB design achieves a functional coverage of 67.4% by hitting 31 out of 46 bins.

extra_quotes: Run the test with Verilator. After every successful simulation, merge the new coverage into a running result with a per-bin max(), so a bin once hit is never lost; this is the union-merge idea of UCIS [Accellera Systems Initiative, 2012].

(i) The LLM-generated directed tests are not independently checked in the loop. Only one test was checked by hand with the monitor. A test can close coverage with invalid stimulus, and we do not measure how often that happens.
(ii) There are three small designs and 12 logged runs from several agent checkpoints, with no fixed-version repeated trials, no confidence intervals and no pass@k.
(iii) There is no baseline, such as plain random re-seeding, a scripted strategy, or another LLM system, and no ablation of the single-bin target,LESSONS.md or clean_code().

(v) The base testbenches are hand-built per design, so the agent’s input is not free. Base coverage therefore describes our testbenches, not a measured random-stimulus plateau; the 1000-seed runs mentioned above checked data integrity, not coverage.
(vi) If clean_code() rejects the output, for example on a syntax error, the iteration is skipped and the model is not told why.
